event.summary: Launch excerpts remain fenced to the failed host's final output
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether removing the asynchronous tmux capture fence could quote a running or previous agent's screen as the launch failure. Source checks refute that route: append_launch_excerpt at lines 59-78 requires HostEvidence::Owned { dead: true }; hosts/terminal.rs:838-850 returns that evidence only for Liveness::Exited, after the processed exit record, and each host runs only one child. status.rs:630-652 calls it only after the dead terminal/unconsumed spec/no-sentinel classification; handlers.rs:988-1044 waits for final state before that inference. SPEC_impl.md:2219-2235 states: 'A launch that never started is classified, and quoted from the emulator’s screen ... only once the host’s exit record has been processed'; its Launch failure classification at 2752-2766 also requires final-screen output and a blank new screen after Restart. This is source-supported, not execution-observed. Suggested bucket if real: other (incorrect diagnostic); could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work consequence. Confidence: confirmed refutation of this proposed route. proposed_drop: code refutes it through final exit evidence and per-host child identity. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not prove every host/runtime transition in neighboring groups; this record covers the excerpt helper and its two callers.

event.summary: Final exit evidence fences the excerpt without relying on a bare child PID
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333; synthesis cross-check at range tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. TLDR: the moved excerpt helper does not classify a merely reaped child as a completed failed terminal, and cannot quote a previous host run. New checks: current handlers.rs:864-912 uses probe only to select the lifecycle branch and captures the adoption-pinned sweep root immediately for a live child; its dead-child path at 988-1044 waits for holds_final_state before inferring a startup failure. Current status.rs:562-636 instead derives terminal_dead from HostEvidence, not the process-table probe. HostStatus::evidence at terminal.rs:838-850 marks dead only for the processed Exited record; Runtime::on_exited at 3914-3923 flushes any synchronized update and publishes the screen before setting Exited. The excerpt's own fresh evidence check still requires dead at launch_artifacts.rs:68-72. A later diff check showed these semantics and both caller paths unchanged through the tip; only unrelated wire/report metadata changed. Source caveat clarified: terminal.rs:3911-3913 explicitly says output after the child exit from descendants retaining the pty is still fed, so 'final screen' does not mean an immutable frozen frame forever. That does not redirect this helper to a different launch: the HostTerminal handle still owns one host/child lifetime, and Restart creates another host rather than reusing it. Exact governing SPEC_impl.md text at 2759-2763: 'A host runs one child for its whole life, so everything on its screen is this launch’s output; the screen is quoted only once the host’s exit record has been processed, which follows the child’s drained output, and a Restart’s new host starts with a blank screen, so no quote reaches back into the previous run.' The original quote risk remains refuted by source rather than by an assumed immutable screen or a pid-liveness test. Suggested bucket if real: other (incorrect diagnostic); could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work consequence. Confidence: confirmed refutation of the stated attribution/premature-quote route, source-only. proposed_drop: code refutes it through processed exit evidence and per-host launch identity. possible_cover: none. No execution. This does not assert that every asynchronous classification outside the excerpt helper has been reviewed.

event.summary: Check resize promotion of inherited Restart history into a launch-error excerpt
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. New cross-group input from g013/f2:11 reports that alacritty grow_lines can promote inherited Restart history into the initially blank screen when a viewer increases height, before the new login shell consumes its launch spec; a later shell startup failure would then quote those previous-run rows. This is a concrete conditional route that invalidates a global refutation based only on one-child host identity and a blank seed. Original c1 consequence retained: a failed launch may quote previous-run messages as its own diagnostic; earlier proposed_drop basis was processed final-exit evidence plus per-host lifetime identity. That basis proves the timing/lifetime boundaries but does not yet exclude imported history moving onto the visible screen. Checks pending: exact seed/reflow behavior, viewer-attach publication ordering, unread spec and later failure path, whole pinned-range attribution and explicit acceptance wording. g013 owns the broader behavior/promise-introduction investigation; this group will inspect only the helper's contract/caller interaction and revise this original ID. Suggested bucket: other for incorrect diagnostic unless a stronger route is established; could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work consequence. Confidence: source-conditional lead from another group, not yet independently settled here. proposed_drop: false pending checks; no parent drop accepted. possible_cover: g013/f2 may be the same contamination cause; exact deduplication belongs to parent. event.summary: Resize can promote inherited Restart history into the failed launch's quoted screen
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: after Restart, increasing terminal height while the login shell is still starting can make a later startup error quote a previous run's message as that failed launch's last output. This is a source-confirmed conditional interaction, not observed execution. Details: the seed intentionally carries old primary history above a blank visible screen (terminal-emulator snapshot/v1/mod.rs:242-268). Vendor grid/resize.rs:25-28 invokes grow_lines for a height increase; :46-71 promotes min(history_size, lines_added) history rows into the visible grid. term/mod.rs:756-758 enables that primary-grid resize. host_launch.rs:508-518 supplies initial_snapshot to the new host, :579-625 waits for host readiness/adoption, then :639-645 tracks the still-pending launch spec and returns. host_restart.rs:294-305 confirms the socket; :363-388 publishes it before returning, without waiting for the login shell to consume its launch spec. Thus a viewer may resize this new terminal during ordinary shell initialization; handlers.rs:2081 forwards owned viewer resizes to the resolved HostTerminal, whose resize request/record is applied to the emulator (terminal.rs:3872-3885,4063-4070). If the shell subsequently exits without consuming the spec or overwriting all promoted rows, status.rs:630-652 recognizes the unconsumed-spec/no-sentinel failure and calls the excerpt helper. screen.rs:50-96 includes those visible rows, and launch_artifacts.rs:97-105 selects the last five nonblank rows, so blank rows below the promoted old output do not protect attribution. No row provenance check distinguishes inherited history from this launch's output. The helper still requires processed exit evidence; that proves output ordering, not provenance of cells imported by the seed. Original c1 consequence and earlier proposed-drop basis preserved: the concern was quoting a running/previous agent's screen, and earlier revisions proposed a drop based on processed final-exit evidence, one-child host lifetime and blank Restart seed. Those checks correctly refute premature process-probe quoting, but do not refute this history-promotion route; the general source-refuted conclusion is withdrawn. Contract: SPEC.md:2890-2893 requires omitting an excerpt that cannot safely be attributed to the launch. SPEC_impl.md:2759-2763 and the newly rewritten helper docstring at :44-56 claim the blank new screen prevents quotes from previous runs; resize makes that invariant false. Remedy direction: track inherited-history provenance through promotion, or conservatively omit the excerpt once inherited content may have entered the screen. Whole-range attribution checked: the excluded base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a already has the same host screen quote and blank-seed rationale in launch_artifacts.rs:52-101; grid/resize.rs has no diff from that base to this commit, and only comments differ in the history encoder. Therefore do not claim this helper move newly introduced the runtime route. The assigned rewrite retains/reasserts the false attribution rationale while moving the helper, and g013/f2 independently owns the later in-range SPEC caveat-removal/promise change at f96dd4363d97dc7e07dea5b8947c96be6bf912e8. Parent should reconcile that shared cause and attribution rather than count this as a separate newly introduced bug. Suggested bucket: other (misleading durable launch diagnostic). Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed conditional source/control-flow route; requires retained old history, a height increase after publication and before classification, and shell startup failure leaving a promoted row visible. No special seam, second failure or runtime reproduction was used. proposed_drop: false; earlier proposed source refutation is withdrawn and no parent drop accepted. possible_cover: g013/f2 is the same source contamination route; no forbidden coverage sources searched. Distinct l1 bounded excerpt-copying finding remains unchanged. No unresolved readily checkable premise remains for this conditional route.

event.summary: Check transient cost of the new excerpt reducer on a maximum-size screen
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: a failed launch with a very wide terminal may make the supervisor allocate and escape far more text than the 500-byte diagnostic retains. The new helper collects all row slices, then builds all five retained rows before trimming. The removed implementation at parent tmux.rs:180-299 bounded each line and pending whitespace incrementally. Source checks made so far: the patch, old reducer, two call sites and final-exit contract; no execution. Exact missing premise: the maximum terminal dimensions and text per cell exposed by screen_tail, and whether that creates a material incremental resource cost beyond the already-required screen read. Next check: host dimension limit, emulator screen-tail implementation and input size admission. Suggested bucket: other unless a material host-wide impact is established; could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route. Confidence: unresolved lead, not a finding. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. No runtime reproduction is requested or planned.

event.summary: Excerpt reduction has finite extra cost; no material regression established
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: investigated whether the replacement reducer could cause unbounded allocations when a launch fails; the suspected unbounded route is refuted. Checks: protocol.rs:100-145 caps each dimension at 10,000; screen.rs:50-96 emits one line per row and base plus combining marks per cell; vendor/alacritty_terminal/src/term/cell.rs:46-56,362-368 caps combining marks at 16 per cell; hosts/terminal.rs:2233-2240 already reads the whole visible screen, as the parent version's append_launch_excerpt did. The new lines vector has at most 10,000 row slices. Escaping copies only five rows, each at most 10,000 cells and 17 characters per cell (at most 8.5 MB of escaped character text before String capacity overhead with the conservative 10-byte escape bound), followed by truncation to 500 bytes. This is more transient copying than the old 500-byte incremental reducer, but bounded and confined to terminal-based launch failure. No source route to a material UX, security or work-loss failure was established beyond the whole-screen extraction that already existed. Suggested bucket if reported: other (bounded transient cost). Could-be-highest: no. Confidence: confirmed bounds from source; no runtime measurements. proposed_drop: source refutes unbounded growth; no established user-facing defect from this bounded extra allocation. possible_cover: none. Original suspected consequence preserved: a very wide failed terminal builds much more than the retained diagnostic; that finite cost remains, but this review does not claim it causes a failure. Lead settled; no missing premise needed to decide the unbounded-growth concern.

event.summary: Reassess the bounded excerpt-copying regression against explicit resource contracts
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Synthesis correction: the original concern was extra allocation and escaping far beyond a 500-byte diagnostic, not only unboundedness. The previous candidate disposition proved finite dimensions but did not by itself refute that bounded resource regression. Preserve the established consequence: the new helper collects all screen-row slices and copies and escapes the five retained rows before trimming, whereas the previous reducer retained bounded suffixes while scanning. Supported host dimensions are up to 10,000 by 10,000; the cell limit is 16 combining marks plus a base. The conservative derived upper bound is 8.5 MB of escaped text for five maximally wide rows before String-capacity overhead, separate from the already-existing full-screen extraction. No latency, OOM or work-loss consequence has been measured or established. Checks now needed: applicable explicit emulator/supervisor resource limits and whether they narrow reachable row width, text/escaping bounds and the two callers' scheduling contexts. Suggested bucket: other for the established resource regression unless stronger impact is supported. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed extra copying by source, open contract/disposition check. proposed_drop: false pending this check; the earlier proposed drop has not been accepted. possible_cover: none. Source-only investigation; no execution or reproduction.

event.summary: Launch-error reduction now allocates full rows before enforcing its tiny result limit
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: when a launch fails before its agent starts, assembling its 500-byte error excerpt now makes temporary allocations proportional to the terminal's height and the full width of its last five nonblank rows. The prior reducer kept those temporary text buffers bounded while reading the same full screen. This is a source-confirmed bounded resource regression; this finding does not claim measured latency, OOM or loss of work. Details: launch_excerpt_of_text at lines 97-105 collects every nonblank row slice before selecting five; lines 107-117 append and escape all characters of those five rows; only lines 119-124 trim to LAUNCH_EXCERPT_BYTES=500. The replaced parent tmux.rs:180-299 reducer keeps at most five suffixes, trims line/whitespace buffers on each append, and trims the joined result. The existing full-screen extraction in append_launch_excerpt line 72 and hosts/terminal.rs:2233-2240 remains an independent cost: it does not eliminate this newly added vector and escaped-row allocation. Explicit bounds checked: terminal-host protocol.rs:100-145 permits 10,000 columns and 10,000 rows; host_launch.rs:513-514 clamps creates to that bound, not to the ordinary 200-column measurement size. screen.rs:50-96 emits one row per screen row and base plus combining marks; vendor cell.rs:46-56,362-368 caps marks at 16 per cell. Therefore row references are bounded by 10,000, and a conservative ceiling for the five-row temporary string is 5*10,000*17*10+12 = 8,500,012 bytes of escaped text before String-capacity overhead (10 is the maximum char::escape_default spelling length, 12 the four separators). That is an upper bound, not a claim every cell can simultaneously realize that spelling; ignored-format filtering and the 64 MiB extra-storage cap can narrow content. The ordinary 80 MiB / hostile about 190 MiB memory figures in SPEC_impl.md:2869-2878 and emulator lib.rs:47-104 are conditional on 200 columns and full scrollback, not a separate global width admission limit. The 500-byte excerpt contract at SPEC_impl.md:2756-2766 is still met by the returned text; no hard RSS-limit breach is alleged. The two callers run synchronously within async observation/Stop processing (status.rs:652; handlers.rs:1039), so the extra work is paid by those paths, but its wall time was not measured and material user-visible latency is not asserted. A correction can retain only the suffix needed for the escaped 500-byte result and the last five nonblank rows, as the prior reducer did, without changing output. Suggested bucket: other, for the established bounded allocation/work regression; could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route. Confidence: confirmed from source; no execution. proposed_drop: false (supersedes the earlier proposed drop based only on finite bounds and lack of an observed failure). possible_cover: none. Caveats: full-screen extraction predates this patch; this is neither an unbounded-memory finding nor a claim that the documented terminal memory budgets are necessarily exceeded.

event.summary: The host-only probe still preserves adoption-pinned identity through Stop's async sweep
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333; caller synthesis checked at 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db, whose relevant HostStatus/probe/sweep_root semantics have not changed. TLDR: considered whether changing the test and host-only interface from TerminalProbe::Owned to TerminalProbe::Running(pid) loses process identity, so Stop could later kill an unrelated process that reused the child's PID, or an unreadable host could falsely report its tree cleaned. Current source refutes that route. HostStatus::pinned_child at hosts/terminal.rs:791-799 compares the process table with the root/start time pinned at adoption. Its probe at 818-832 returns a bare PID only after that check; live_root at 737-751 refuses Unavailable and process-read failures, and HostTerminal::sweep_root at 2571-2583 reuses the pinned root and checks its PID against the probe. handlers.rs:864-912 captures that root before durable I/O and refuses on errors. sweep.rs:2008-2035 carries the pair through recording StopRequested into reap_process_tree; reap_process_tree_with_sweep at 1431-1439 revalidates it after the async gap. validate_root_identity/root_from_read at 1574-1625 admits only the same start time, drops a missing or changed identity, and returns an error on an unreadable process row. Delete intentionally differs from Stop: session_hosts.rs:510-541 uses pinned_child_root or a fresh over-connection pin_child for known hosts, so an unavailable host need not hide a still-running child; HostStatus::pinned_child_root at terminal.rs:773-784 still matches adoption start identity before returning it. The changed test continues to force unreadability after the probe and requires sweep_root(live).is_err(). This conclusion is source-supported, not execution-observed. Suggested bucket if the suspected route existed: highest, because it could kill unrelated user processes; could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed refutation of the bare-PID/async-gap route. proposed_drop: source refutes the route via adoption-pinned start identities, immediate root capture, and revalidation; no specification exception is needed for this refutation. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this is not a claim to eliminate the distinct non-atomic read/signal race or globally equal start timestamps; those were not the suspected regression here. Parent owns any independent drop check; no drop has been accepted by the parent.

HostStatus::pinned_child (terminal.rs:791-799) compares the process table with the adoption-pinned root/start time; probe (818-832) returns its PID, live_root (737-751) refuses unreadability, and sweep_root (2571-2583) returns the pinned pair after checking the probe PID. Stop captures that pair before its durable write (handlers.rs:864-912); Restart captures it before settle_outstanding_launches can wait and passes it to stop_live_agent (core.rs:12336-12417); tab cleanup probes and captures it before reap_tab_processes (core.rs:14072-14123). stop_live_agent carries the pair through its StopRequested write (sweep.rs:2008-2035). The shared reap revalidates every root after those awaits (1431-1439); validate_root_identity/root_from_read (1574-1625) drops changed/missing identities and refuses unreadable rows. Delete intentionally bypasses the live-host requirement but preserves identity: teardown.rs:320-344 uses pinned_child_root for the agent, session_hosts.rs:510-541 uses it for tab runtimes or pin_child over a recorded host's connection, and HostStatus::pinned_child_root (terminal.rs:773-784) still requires the adoption-pinned start time. Thus a stopped/unreadable host does not hide its still-identical child from unconditional Delete; a guarded Delete refuses that uncertainty earlier. The changed test retains its after-probe unreadability transition and requires sweep_root(live).is_err(). Suggested bucket if the suspected route existed: highest, because unrelated user processes could be killed; could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source refutation, no execution. proposed_drop: code refutes the bare-PID/async-gap route with pinned start identities, root capture before async work, and shared revalidation; no specification exception is needed. possible_cover: none.
